data.title: Malicious Network Driver for Persistence
data.summary: The sample installs a kernel-level network driver or filter that gives it a persistent vantage point over network traffic — for interception, covert channel use, or onward lateral movement — independent of user-mode networking controls.
data.description:
A network filter driver sits below most host-based network monitoring and user-mode
firewall controls, which is why this technique both persists reliably and evades
detection tooling that only observes traffic at the socket or application layer. It is
often used specifically to establish a covert communication channel that bypasses
conventional egress filtering, or to pivot onward to other hosts on the same network
segment with reduced visibility.
data.recommendation:
* Enumerate installed network filter drivers (NDIS filters, WFP callout drivers) against a known-good baseline, since this layer is invisible to most user-mode network monitoring.
* Capture traffic at a network tap or span port outside the host's own control, rather than relying on host-based capture the driver itself could be filtering.
* Treat confirmed presence as evidence of both persistence and an active covert channel, and scope lateral-movement investigation to the same network segment.
data.short_recommendation: Enumerate network filter drivers directly; this layer is invisible to most user-mode network monitoring and host-based capture.

mitre_techniques.technique: T1543 — Create or Modify System Process
mitre_techniques.procedure: Installed a Windows Filtering Platform callout driver that redirected a subset of outbound traffic through an operator-controlled relay.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Network filter driver provided a persistent, kernel-level vantage point for covert traffic redirection.
